reviewed_by: Claude Opus 5 (Claude Code session 2026-07-26), blind packet-only re-review triggered by the validate_judgment staleness gate

samples_reviewed.question_text: A square is cut on a slant, from one edge to another. What two shapes are made?
Two triangles are placed together, matching their longest straight edges. What shape do they form?
A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?
A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?
Two triangles are placed together, matching their longest straight edges. What shape do they form?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Seeds 44 and 45 render 'A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?' with 'two squares' marked correct and 'two rectangles' marked incorrect. Halving a general rectangle yields two rectangles; only the special case where the length is exactly twice the width yields squares, and the stem specifies no such dimensions, so the keyed answer is wrong and the correct answer is scored as a distractor.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Composition (two triangles forming a rectangle) and decomposition (a square cut into two triangles) both appear, so both halves of the compose/decompose competency are represented, but squares are never the composed result and rectangles are never validly decomposed.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'Two triangles are placed together, matching their longest straight edges' asks a Grade 1 Quarter 1 student to reason about which edge is longest and to mentally join figures without a picture; the purely verbal framing carries more spatial working memory load than a diagram-based item would.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All five seeds use the same mcq presentation and produce only three distinct stems; no variant asks the student to select the pieces that compose a given figure, which is the other natural orientation of this competency.

competency_alignment.rationale: Because the rectangle-halving item is mis-keyed, a student reasoning correctly is marked wrong on two of five sampled generations, so the difficulty progression actively penalises mastery of the competency rather than building it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: There is no numeric magnitude axis in this competency; the item space is the small set of triangles, squares and rectangles the competency names, and the samples do not reach beyond that set.
